Triangle Notation

  • aa = minimum
  • bb = maximum
  • cc = mode
  • hh = density at the mode = 2b−a\frac{2}{b-a}

Triangle Probability Density Funciton (PDF)

Lemma 1: (Triangle PDF).

Given, x,a,b,c∈ℝx, a, b, c \in \mathbb{R}and a≤c<ba \le c \lt bor a<c≤ba \lt c \le bthe triangle probability density function is given by

f(x)={2(b−a)(c−a)(x−a)if a≤x≤c2(b−a)(c−b)(x−b)if c<x≤b0otherwise \begin{equation} f(x) = \begin{cases} \frac{2}{(b-a)(c-a)}(x-a) & \mbox{if } a \leq x \leq c \\ \frac{2}{(b-a)(c-b)}(x-b) & \mbox{if } c < x \leq b \\ 0 & \mbox{otherwise} \end{cases} \end{equation}

if a random variable X has a PDF f(x), then we say X∼triangle(a,b,c)X \sim triangle(a, b, c)

Proof

The triangle is made of two lines:

(y−0)=h−0c−a(x−a)(y-0) = \frac{h-0}{c-a}(x-a)

(y−0)=h−0c−b(x−b)(y-0)=\frac{h-0}{c-b}(x-b)

Integrating the pdf under these two equations to solve for hh:

∫f(x)dx=1\int f(x) dx = 1

hc−a∫ac(x−a)dx+hc−b∫cb(x−b)dx=h(b−a)2=1\frac{h}{c-a}\int_{a}^{c} (x-a) dx + \frac{h}{c-b} \int_{c}^{b} (x-b) dx = \frac{h(b-a)}{2} = 1

h=2b−ah=\frac{2}{b-a}

The PDF should be zero at each end of the interval and be continuous at cc

f(a)=2(b−a)(c−a)(a−a)=0f(a) = \frac{2}{(b-a)(c-a)}(a-a) = 0

f(b)=2(b−a)(c−b)(b−b)f(b) = \frac{2}{(b-a)(c-b)}(b-b)

fa≤x≤c(c)=2(b−a)(c−a)(c−a)=2(b−a)f_{a \le x \le c}(c) = \frac{2}{(b-a)(c-a)}(c-a) = \frac{2}{(b-a)}

limx→cfc<x≤b(x)=limx→c2(b−a)(c−b)(x−b)=2(b−a)\lim_{x \to c} f_{c \lt x \le b}(x) = \lim_{x \to c} \frac{2}{(b-a)(c-b)}(x-b) = \frac{2}{(b-a)}

Triangle Cumulative Distribution Function (CDF)

Lemma 2: (Triangle CDF).

Given, x,a,b,c∈ℝx, a, b, c \in \mathbb{R}and a≤c<ba \le c \lt bor a<c≤ba \lt c \le bthe cumulative distribution function over xxis

F(x)={0if x<a(x−a)2(b−a)(c−a)if a≤x≤c1+(x−b)2(b−a)(c−b)if c<x≤b1if x>b \begin{equation} F(x) = \begin{cases} 0 & \mbox{if } x < a \\ \frac{(x-a)^2}{(b-a)(c-a)} & \mbox{if } a \leq x \leq c \\ 1 + \frac{(x-b)^2}{(b-a)(c-b)} & \mbox{if } c < x \leq b \\ 1 & \mbox{if } x > b \end{cases} \end{equation}

Proof

F(x)=∫−∞xf(t)dtF(x) = \int_{-\infty}^{x} f(t) dt

Fa≤x≤c(x)=∫ax2(t−a)(b−a)(c−a)dt=(x−a)2(b−a)(c−a) \begin{align} F_{a \le x \le c}(x) &= \int_a^x \frac{2(t-a)}{(b-a)(c-a)} dt \\ &= \frac{(x-a)^2}{(b-a)(c-a)} \end{align}

Fc<x<b(x)=Fa≤x≤c(c)+∫cx2(t−b)(b−a)(c−b)dt=1−∫xb2(t−b)(b−a)(c−b)dt=1+(x−b)2(b−a)(c−b)=1−(b−x)2(b−a)(b−c) \begin{align} F_{c \lt x \lt b}(x) &= F_{a \le x \le c}(c) + \int_c^x \frac{2(t-b)}{(b-a)(c-b)} dt = 1 - \int_x^b \frac{2(t-b)}{(b-a)(c-b)} dt \\ &= 1 + \frac{(x - b)^2}{(b-a)(c-b)} = 1 - \frac{(b - x)^2}{(b-a)(b - c)} \end{align}

The CDF should be zero at aa, continuous at cc, and one at bb

Fa≤x≤c(a)=(a−a)2(b−a)(c−a)=0F_{a \le x \le c}(a) = \frac{(a-a)^2}{(b-a)(c-a)} = 0

Fc<x<b(b)=1−(b−b)2(b−a)(b−c)=1F_{c \lt x \lt b}(b) = 1 - \frac{(b - b)^2}{(b-a)(b - c)} = 1

Fa≤x≤c(c)=(c−a)2(b−a)(c−a)=(c−a)(b−a)F_{a \le x \le c}(c) = \frac{(c-a)^2}{(b-a)(c-a)} = \frac{(c-a)}{(b-a)}

limx→cFc<x<b(c)=limx→c[1−(b−x)2(b−a)(b−c)]=1−(b−c)(b−a)=(c−a)(b−a)\lim_{x \to c} F_{c \lt x \lt b}(c) = \lim_{x \to c} \left[ 1 - \frac{(b - x)^2}{(b-a)(b - c)} \right] = 1 - \frac{(b - c)}{(b-a)} = \frac{(c-a)}{(b-a)}

Triangle Mean

Lemma 3: (Triangle Mean).

The mean of the triangle distribution is

E(X)=a+b+c3E(X) = \frac{a+b+c}{3}

Proof

E(X)=∫xf(x)dx=2(b−a)(c−a)∫ac(x2−ax)dx+2(b−a)(c−b)∫cb(x2−bx)dx=2(b−a)(c−a)[13x3−a2x2]ac+2(b−a)(c−b)[13x2−b2x2]cbdx=a+b+c3 \begin{align} E(X) &= \int xf(x)dx = \frac{2}{(b-a)(c-a)}\int_a^c (x^2-ax) dx + \frac{2}{(b-a)(c-b)}\int_c^b (x^2-bx) dx \\ &= \frac{2}{(b-a)(c-a)} \left[\frac{1}{3}x^3-\frac{a}{2}x^2\right]_a^c + \frac{2}{(b-a)(c-b)}\left[\frac{1}{3}x^2-\frac{b}{2}x^2\right]_c^b dx \\ &= \frac{a+b+c}{3} \end{align}

Triangle Variance

Lemma 4: (Triangle Variance).

The variance of the triangle distribution is

V(X)=a2+b2+c2−ab−ac−bc18V(X) = \frac{a^2+b^2+c^2-ab-ac-bc}{18}

Proof

V(X)=E(X2)−(E(X))2=∫x2f(x)dx−(a+b+c3)2=2(b−a)(c−a)∫acx2(x−a)dx+2(b−a)(c−b)∫cbx2(x−b)dx−(a+b+c3)2=2(b−a)(c−a)[14x4−a3x3]ac+2(b−a)(c−b)[14x4−b3x3]cb−(a+b+c3)2=a2+b2+c2−ab−ac−bc18 \begin{align} V(X) &= E(X^2) - \big(E(X)\big)^2 = \int x^2f(x)dx- \bigg(\frac{a+b+c}{3}\bigg)^2 \\ &= \frac{2}{(b-a)(c-a)}\int_{a}^{c} x^2(x-a) dx + \frac{2}{(b-a)(c-b)} \int_{c}^{b} x^2(x-b) dx- \bigg(\frac{a+b+c}{3}\bigg)^2 \\ &= \frac{2}{(b-a)(c-a)} \left[\frac{1}{4}x^4-\frac{a}{3}x^3\right]_a^c + \frac{2}{(b-a)(c-b)}\left[\frac{1}{4}x^4-\frac{b}{3}x^3\right]_c^b - \bigg(\frac{a+b+c}{3}\bigg)^2 \\ &= \frac{a^2+b^2+c^2-ab-ac-bc}{18} \end{align}

Method of Moments Estimation

The Type 1 and 2 notation is used in the package, but are not externally accepted “types” of Methods of Moments.

Type 1

Lemma 5: (Method of Moments Estimator 1).

Estimators for the Triangle parameters are

â=min(x)=X(1)\hat{a} = min(x) = X_{(1)}

b̂=max(x)=X(n)\hat{b} = max(x) = X_{(n)}

ĉ=3x‾−min⁡(x)−max⁡(x)\hat{c} = 3\bar{x} - \min(x) - \max(x)

Motivation

E(X)=a+b+c3E(X) = \frac{a + b + c}{3}

c=3E(X)−a−bc = 3E(X) - a - b

The sample minimum is an overestimate for aa and the sample maximum is an underestimate for bb.

ĉ\hat{c} is a biased estimator for cc.

E(ĉ)=3E(x‾)−E(X(1))−E(X(n))=3n∑i=1nE(Xi)−n[∑k=0n−1(n−1k)(c−ab−a)n−k(−1)n−1−k2c(n−k)+a(n−k)(2(n−k)+1)−(b−cb−a)n2cn+bn(2n+1)]−n[(c−ab−a)n2cn+an(2n+1)+∑k=0n−1(n−1k)(c−bb−a)n−k2c(n−k)+b(n−k)(2(n−k)+1)]=a+b+c−[expansion]−[expansion]≠c \begin{align} E(\hat{c}) =& 3E(\bar{x}) - E(X_{(1)}) - E(X_{(n)}) \\ =& \frac{3}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n E(X_i) \\ &- n \left[\sum_{k=0}^{n-1} {n-1 \choose k} \left(\frac{c-a}{b-a}\right)^{n-k} (-1)^{n-1-k} \frac{2c(n-k)+a}{(n-k)(2(n-k) + 1)} - \left(\frac{b-c}{b-a}\right)^n \frac{2cn+b}{n(2n+1)} \right] \\ &- n \left[ \left(\frac{c-a}{b-a}\right)^n \frac{2cn+a}{n(2n + 1)} + \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} {n-1 \choose k} \left(\frac{c-b}{b-a}\right)^{n-k} \frac{2c(n-k)+b}{(n-k)(2(n-k)+1)} \right] \\ =& a + b + c - [expansion] - [expansion]\\ \neq & c \end{align}

Simulation shows that ĉ\hat{c} is consistent for cc.

Type 2

Lemma 6: (Method of Moments Estimator 2).

Estimators for the Triangle parameters are the solution to these equations for the mean, variance, and skewness

x‾=1n∑ixi=â+b̂+ĉ3\bar{x} = \frac{1}{n} \sum_i x_i = \frac{\hat{a} + \hat{b} + \hat{c}}{3}

1n−1∑i(xi−x‾)2=â2+b̂2+ĉ2−âb̂−âĉ−b̂ĉ18\frac{1}{n-1} \sum_i (x_i - \bar{x})^2 = \frac{\hat{a}^2+\hat{b}^2+\hat{c}^2-\hat{a}\hat{b}-\hat{a}\hat{c}-\hat{b}\hat{c}}{18}

n∑i(xi−x‾)3[∑i(xi−x‾)2]3/2=2(â+b̂−2ĉ)(2â−b̂−ĉ)(â−2b̂+ĉ)5(â2+b̂2+ĉ2−âb̂−âĉ−b̂ĉ)3/2\frac{\sqrt{n} \sum_i (x_i-\bar{x})^3}{\left[\sum_i (x_i-\bar{x})^2\right]^{3/2}} = \frac{\sqrt{2} (\hat{a} + \hat{b} - 2\hat{c}) (2\hat{a} - \hat{b} - \hat{c}) (\hat{a} - 2\hat{b} + \hat{c})}{5(\hat{a}^2+\hat{b}^2+\hat{c}^2-\hat{a}\hat{b}-\hat{a}\hat{c}-\hat{b}\hat{c})^{3/2}}

Maximum Likelihood Estimation

The procedure for maximum likelihood estimation involves maximizing the likelihood with respect to cc for a fixed aa and bb, followed by minimizing the negative log likelihood with respect to aa and bb for a fixed cc.

Maximizing the Likelihood with respect to cc (given aa and bb)

This discussion follows the results from Samuel Kotz and Johan Rene van Dorp. Beyond Beta

For the purposes of this section, with a fixed aa and bb, the sample can be easily rescaled to a=0a=0 and b=1b=1. This section will proceed on [0,1][0,1] with the mode at 0≤c≤10 \le c \le 1

w(x)={2xcif 0≤x<c2(1−x)1−cif c≤x≤10otherwisew(x) = \left\{ \begin{array}{ll} \frac{2x}{c} & \mbox{if } 0 \le x \lt c \\ \frac{2(1-x)}{1-c} & \mbox{if } c \le x \leq 1 \\ 0 & \mbox{otherwise} \end{array} \right.

L(x|c)=∏inw(x|c)L(x|c) = \prod_{i}^{n} w(x|c)

Assume that the sample is ordered into order statistics X(1)<…<X(n)X_{(1)} \lt \dots \lt X_{(n)}. Also, note that X(r)≤c<X(r+1)X_{(r)} \le c \lt X_{(r+1)}. In other words, the mode falls between the rthr^{th} and r+1r+1 order statistics.

L(x|c)=∏i=1r2x(i)c∏i=r+1n2(1−x(i))1−c=2n∏i=1rx(i)∏i=r+1n(1−x(i))cr(1−c)n−rL(x|c) = \prod_{i=1}^{r} \frac{2x_{(i)}}{c} \prod_{i=r+1}^{n} \frac{2(1-x_{(i)})}{1-c} = \frac{2^n \prod_{i=1}^{r} x_{(i)} \prod_{i=r+1}^{n} (1-x_{(i)})}{c^r(1-c)^{n-r}}

To maximize the likelihood, we can first maximize with respect to rr and then locate cc between the rthr^{th} and r+1r+1 order statistics. For notation purposes, also define X(0)=0X_{(0)} = 0 and X(n+1)=1X_{(n+1)} = 1.

$$\large \max_{0 \le c \le 1} L(x|c) = \max_{r \ \epsilon \ (0,\dots,n)} \ \ \max_{x_{(r)} \le c \le x_{(r+1)}} \ \ L(x|c)$$

Case 1: cc is between the first and second to last order statistic rϵ(1,…,n−1)r \ \epsilon \ (1, \dots, n-1)

Noticing that maximizing the likelihood is equivalent to minimizing the denominator:

$$\large \max L(x|c) = \max_{r \ \epsilon \ (1,\dots,n-1)} \ \ \min_{x_{(r)} \le c \le x_{(r+1)}} \ \ c^r(1-c)^{n-r}$$

Since cr(1−c)n−rc^r(1-c)^{n-r} is unimodal with respect to cc, it should be sufficient to test the end points of an interval to find the minimum on the interval

$$\large = \max_{r \ \epsilon \ (1,\dots,n-1)} \ \ \min_{c \ \epsilon \ (x_{(r)},\ \ x_{(r+1)})} \ \ c^r(1-c)^{n-r}$$

Therefore, for this case, it is sufficient to test the likelihood using cc at each of the sampled points and find the largest.

Side note on z=cr(1−c)n−rz=c^r(1-c)^{n-r} being unimodal

dzdc=rc(r−1)(1−c)n−r+cr(n−r)(1−c)n−r−1(−1)=c(r−1)(1−c)n−r−1(r−cn)\frac{dz}{dc} = rc^{(r-1)}(1-c)^{n-r} + c^r(n-r)(1-c)^{n-r-1}(-1) = c^{(r-1)}(1-c)^{n-r-1}(r - cn)

dzdc=0\frac{dz}{dc} = 0 at c=0,1,rnc=0,\ 1,\ \frac{r}{n}. At 0<c<rn0 < c < \frac{r}{n}, zz is positive, and at rn<c<1\frac{r}{n} < c < 1, zz is negative. Therefore, zz is unimodal on (0,1)(0,1).

Case 2: cc is between 0 and the first order statistic r=0r = 0

$$\large \max L(x|c) = \max_{0 \le c \le x_{(1)}} \prod_{i=1}^{n} \frac{1-x_{(i)}}{1-c} = \prod_{i=1}^{n} \frac{1-x_{(i)}}{1-x_{(1)}}$$

Choosing the largest endpoint in the interval, creates the smallest denominator, and the largest likelihood.

Therefore, for this case, it is sufficient to test the likelihood using cc at the first sampled point.

Case 3: cc is between the last order statistic r=nr = n and 1

$$\large \max L(x|c) = \max_{x_{(n)} \le c \le 1} \prod_{i=1}^{n} \frac{x_{(i)}}{c} = \prod_{i=1}^{n} \frac{x_{(i)}}{x_{(n)}}$$

Choosing the smallest option in the denominator creates the largest likelihood. Again, it is sufficient to test the likelihood using cc at the largest sample point.

All Cases

For all cases, it is sufficient to compute the sample likelihood using cc equal to each of the samples, and choosing the largest likelihood from the nn options to find the corresponding cc. This calculation is performed with a fixed aa and bb, so the test must be performed iteratively as aa and bb are separately optimized.

Negative Log Likelihood

nLL=−log⁡(L)=−log⁡(∏inf(xi))=−∑inlog⁡(f(xi))=−∑i:a≤xi<cn1log⁡(f(xi))−∑i:c≤xi≤bn2log⁡(f(xi)) \begin{align} nLL &= -\log(L) = -\log\left(\prod_i^n f(x_i)\right) \\ &= - \sum_i^n \log\left(f(x_i)\right) = - \sum_{i: \ a \le x_i \lt c}^{n_1} \log\left(f(x_i)\right) - \sum_{i: \ c \le x_i \le b}^{n_2} \log\left(f(x_i)\right) \end{align}

where n=n1+n2n = n_1 + n_2

Case 1: a=c<ba = c \lt b

nLL=−∑inlog⁡(2)+log⁡(b−xi)−log⁡(b−a)−log⁡(b−c)=−nlog⁡(2)+nlog⁡(b−a)+nlog⁡(b−c)−∑inlog⁡(b−xi) \begin{align} nLL &= - \sum_{i}^{n} \log(2) + \log(b-x_i) - \log(b-a) - \log(b-c) \\ &= -n\log(2) + n\log(b-a) + n \log(b-c) - \sum_{i}^{n} \log(b-x_i) \end{align}

Case 2: a<c=ba \lt c = b

nLL=−∑inlog⁡(2)+log⁡(xi−a)−log⁡(b−a)−log⁡(c−a)=−nlog⁡(2)+nlog⁡(b−a)+nlog⁡(c−a)−∑inlog⁡(xi−a) \begin{align} nLL &= - \sum_{i}^{n} \log(2) + \log(x_i - a) - \log(b-a) - \log(c-a) \\ &= -n\log(2) + n\log(b-a) + n\log(c-a) - \sum_{i}^{n} \log(x_i - a) \end{align}

Case 3: a<c<ba \lt c \lt b

nLL=−∑i:a<xi<cn1log⁡(2)+log⁡(xi−a)−log⁡(b−a)−log⁡(c−a)−∑i:c≤xi<bn2log⁡(2)+log⁡(b−xi)−log⁡(b−a)−log⁡(b−c)=−nlog⁡(2)+nlog⁡(b−a)+n1log⁡(c−a)+n2log⁡(b−c)−∑i:a<xi<cn1log⁡(xi−a)−∑i:c≤xi<bn2log⁡(b−xi) \begin{align} nLL &= - \sum_{i: \ a \lt x_i \lt c}^{n_1} \log(2) + \log(x_i - a) - \log(b-a) - \log(c-a) - \sum_{i: \ c \le x_i \lt b}^{n_2} \log(2) + \log(b-x_i) - \log(b-a) - \log(b-c) \\ &= -n\log(2) + n\log(b-a) + n_1\log(c-a) + n_2 \log(b-c) - \sum_{i: \ a \lt x_i \lt c}^{n_1} \log(x_i - a) - \sum_{i: \ c \le x_i \lt b}^{n_2} \log(b-x_i) \end{align}

Gradient of the negative Log Likelihood Given cc:

The negative log likelihood is not differentiable with respect to cc because the limits of the sum (n1n_1 and n2n_2) are functions of cc. Therefore the gradient and hessian are derived as if cc is fixed.

Case 1: a=c<ba = c \lt b

∂nLL∂a=−nb−a\frac{\partial nLL}{\partial a} = - \frac{n}{b-a}

∂nLL∂b=nb−a+nb−c−∑in1b−xi\frac{\partial nLL}{\partial b} = \frac{n}{b-a} + \frac{n}{b-c} - \sum_i^{n} \frac{1}{b-x_i}

Case 2: a<c=ba \lt c = b

∂nLL∂a=−nb−a−nc−a+∑in1xi−a\frac{\partial nLL}{\partial a} = - \frac{n}{b-a} - \frac{n}{c-a} + \sum_i^{n} \frac{1}{x_i - a}

∂nLL∂b=nb−a\frac{\partial nLL}{\partial b} = \frac{n}{b-a}

Case 3: a<c<ba \lt c \lt b

∂nLL∂a=−nb−a−n1c−a+∑in11xi−a\frac{\partial nLL}{\partial a} = - \frac{n}{b-a} - \frac{n_1}{c-a} + \sum_i^{n_1} \frac{1}{x_i - a}

∂nLL∂b=nb−a+n2b−c−∑in21b−xi\frac{\partial nLL}{\partial b} = \frac{n}{b-a} + \frac{n_2}{b-c} - \sum_i^{n_2} \frac{1}{b-x_i}

Hessian of the negative Log Likelihood Given cc:

Case 1: a=c<ba = c \lt b

∂2nLL∂a2=−n(b−a)2\frac{\partial^2nLL}{\partial a^2} = - \frac{n}{(b-a)^2}

∂2nLL∂b2=−n(b−a)2−n(b−c)2+∑in1(b−xi)2\frac{\partial^2 nLL}{\partial b^2} = -\frac{n}{(b-a)^2} - \frac{n}{(b-c)^2} + \sum_i^{n} \frac{1}{(b-x_i)^2}

∂2nLL∂a∂b=∂2nLL∂b∂a=−n(b−a)2\frac{\partial^2 nLL}{\partial a\partial b} = \frac{\partial^2 nLL}{\partial b\partial a} = - \frac{n}{(b-a)^2}

Case 2: a<c=ba \lt c = b

∂2nLL∂a2=−n(b−a)2−n(c−a)2+∑in1(xi−a)2\frac{\partial^2 nLL}{\partial a^2} = - \frac{n}{(b-a)^2} - \frac{n}{(c-a)^2} + \sum_i^{n} \frac{1}{(x_i - a)^2}

∂2nLL∂b2=−n(b−a)2\frac{\partial^2 nLL}{\partial b^2} = - \frac{n}{(b-a)^2}

∂2nLL∂a∂b=∂2nLL∂b∂a=−n(b−a)2\frac{\partial^2 nLL}{\partial a\partial b} = \frac{\partial^2 nLL}{\partial b\partial a} = - \frac{n}{(b-a)^2}

Case 3: a<c<ba \lt c \lt b

∂2nLL∂a2=−n(b−a)2−n1(c−a)2+∑in11(xi−a)2\frac{\partial^2 nLL}{\partial a^2} = - \frac{n}{(b-a)^2} - \frac{n_1}{(c-a)^2} + \sum_i^{n_1} \frac{1}{(x_i - a)^2}

∂2nLL∂b2=−n(b−a)2−n2(b−c)2+∑in21(b−xi)2\frac{\partial ^2 nLL}{\partial b^2} = -\frac{n}{(b-a)^2} - \frac{n_2}{(b-c)^2} + \sum_i^{n_2} \frac{1}{(b-x_i)^2}

∂2nLL∂a∂b=∂2nLL∂b∂a=−n(b−a)2\frac{\partial ^2 nLL}{\partial a\partial b} = \frac{\partial ^2 nLL}{\partial b\partial a} = - \frac{n}{(b-a)^2}

MLE Variance - Covariance

For the optimization of (a,b)(a,b) given cc, we can use the inverse of the hessian of the negative log likelihood for an estimate of the covariance matrix of â\hat{a} and b̂\hat{b}. For the variance in ĉ\hat{c}, we use the variance of the rthr^{th} order statistic which corresponds to cc. The covariance of (a,b)(a,b) and cc is not computed because the negative log likelihood is not differentiable with respect to cc.

Let HH denote the Hessian matrix, and let H−1[1,1]H^{-1}[1,1] be the V(â)V(\hat{a}), H−1[2,2]H^{-1}[2,2] be the V(b̂)V(\hat{b}), and H−1[1,2]=H−1[2,1]H^{-1}[1,2] = H^{-1}[2,1] be the Cov(â,b̂)Cov(\hat{a}, \hat{b}). Then,

V([â,b̂,ĉ])=[H−1[1,1]H−1[1,2]0H−1[2,1]H−1[2,2]000V(ĉ)] V([\hat{a}, \hat{b}, \hat{c}]) = \begin{bmatrix} H^{-1}[1,1] & H^{-1}[1,2] & 0 \\ H^{-1}[2,1] & H^{-1}[2,2] & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & V(\hat{c}) \\ \end{bmatrix}

rthr^{th} order statistic

f(x(r))=r(nr)f(x)[F(x)]r−1[1−F(x)]n−rf(x_{(r)}) = r {n \choose r} f(x) [F(x)]^{r-1}[1-F(x)]^{n-r}

Expected value of the rthr^{th} order statistic

E(X(r))=∫xf(x(r))dx=∫acxr(nr)2(x−a)(b−a)(c−a)((x−a)2(b−a)(c−a))r−1(1−(x−a)2(b−a)(c−a))n−rdx+∫cbxr(nr)2(x−b)(b−a)(c−b)(1+(x−b)2(b−a)(c−b))r−1(−(x−b)2(b−a)(c−b))n−rdx \begin{align} E(X_{(r)}) &= \int x f(x_{(r)}) dx \\ &= \int_a^c xr {n \choose r} \frac{2(x-a)}{(b-a)(c-a)} \left(\frac{(x-a)^2}{(b-a)(c-a)}\right)^{r-1}\left(1 - \frac{(x-a)^2}{(b-a)(c-a)}\right)^{n-r}dx \\ &+ \int_c^b xr {n \choose r} \frac{2(x-b)}{(b-a)(c-b)} \left(1+\frac{(x-b)^2}{(b-a)(c-b)}\right)^{r-1}\left(- \frac{(x-b)^2}{(b-a)(c-b)}\right)^{n-r}dx \end{align}

To simplify the notation, define:

γ0=2r(nr)\gamma_0 = 2r {n \choose r}

γ1=(b−a)(c−a)\gamma_1 = (b-a)(c-a)

γ2=(b−a)(c−b)\gamma_2 = (b-a)(c-b)

Continuing:

E(X(r))=∫acγ0γ1nx(x−a)2r−1(γ1−(x−a)2)n−rdx+∫cbγ0γ2n(−1)n−rx(x−b)2n−2r+1(γ2+(x−b)2)r−1dxE(X_{(r)}) = \int_a^c \frac{\gamma_0}{\gamma_1^n} x(x-a)^{2r-1} \left(\gamma_1 - (x-a)^2\right)^{n-r}dx + \int_c^b \frac{\gamma_0}{\gamma_2^n} (-1)^{n-r}x(x-b)^{2n-2r+1} \left(\gamma_2 + (x-b)^2\right)^{r-1}dx

By using a binomial expansion, we can prevent having to integrate by parts multiple times.

(a+b)n=∑k=0n(nk)akbn−k(a+b)^n = \sum_{k=0}^n {n \choose k} a^kb^{n-k}

E(X(r))=∫acγ0γ1nx(x−a)2r−1∑k=0n−r(n−rk)γ1k(−1)n−r−k(x−a)2n−2r−2kdx+∫cbγ0γ2n(−1)n−rx(x−b)2n−2r+1∑k=0r−1(r−1k)γ2k(x−b)2r−2−2kdx \begin{align} E(X_{(r)}) &= \int_a^c \frac{\gamma_0}{\gamma_1^n} x(x-a)^{2r-1} \sum_{k=0}^{n-r} {n-r \choose k} \gamma_1^k (-1)^{n-r-k}(x-a)^{2n-2r-2k}dx \\ &+ \int_c^b \frac{\gamma_0}{\gamma_2^n} (-1)^{n-r}x(x-b)^{2n-2r+1} \sum_{k=0}^{r-1} {r-1 \choose k} \gamma_2^k (x-b)^{2r-2-2k}dx \end{align}

E(X(r))=γ0γ1n∑k=0n−r(n−rk)γ1k(−1)n−r−k∫acx(x−a)2n−2k−1dx+γ0γ2n(−1)(n−r)∑k=0r−1(r−1k)γ2k∫cbx(x−b)2n−2k−1dx \begin{align} E(X_{(r)}) &= \frac{\gamma_0}{\gamma_1^n} \sum_{k=0}^{n-r} {n-r \choose k} \gamma_1^k (-1)^{n-r-k}\int_a^c x(x-a)^{2n-2k-1}dx \\ &+ \frac{\gamma_0}{\gamma_2^n} (-1)^{(n-r)} \sum_{k=0}^{r-1} {r-1 \choose k} \gamma_2^k \int_c^b x(x-b)^{2n-2k-1}dx \end{align}

E(X(r))=γ0∑k=0n−r(n−rk)γ1k−n(−1)n−r−k[c(c−a)2n−2k2n−2k−(c−a)2n−2k+1(2n−2k)(2n−2k+1)]+γ0(−1)n−r∑k=0r−1(r−1k)γ2k−n[−c(c−b)2n−2k2n−2k+(c−b)2n−2k+1(2n−2k)(2n−2k+1)] \begin{align} E(X_{(r)}) &= \gamma_0 \sum_{k=0}^{n-r} {n-r \choose k} \gamma_1^{k-n} (-1)^{n-r-k} \left[\frac{c(c-a)^{2n-2k}}{2n-2k} - \frac{(c-a)^{2n-2k+1}}{(2n-2k)(2n-2k+1)}\right] \\ &+ \gamma_0 (-1)^{n-r} \sum_{k=0}^{r-1} {r-1 \choose k} \gamma_2^{k-n} \left[\frac{-c(c-b)^{2n-2k}}{2n-2k}+\frac{(c-b)^{2n-2k+1}}{(2n-2k)(2n-2k+1)}\right] \end{align}

E(X(r))=r(nr)∑k=0n−r(n−rk)(b−a)k−n(c−a)n−k(−1)n−r−k[cn−k−c−a(n−k)(2n−2k+1)]+r(nr)(−1)n−r∑k=0r−1(r−1k)(b−a)k−n(c−b)n−k[−cn−k+c−b(n−k)(2n−2k+1)] \begin{align} E(X_{(r)}) &= r {n \choose r} \sum_{k=0}^{n-r} {n-r \choose k} (b-a)^{k-n} (c-a)^{n-k} (-1)^{n-r-k} \left[\frac{c}{n-k} - \frac{c-a}{(n-k)(2n-2k+1)}\right] \\ &+ r {n \choose r} (-1)^{n-r} \sum_{k=0}^{r-1} {r-1 \choose k} (b-a)^{k-n} (c-b)^{n-k} \left[\frac{-c}{n-k}+\frac{c-b}{(n-k)(2n-2k+1)}\right] \end{align}

E(X(r))=r(nr)[∑k=0n−r(n−rk)(b−a)k−n(c−a)n−k(−1)n−r−k2c(n−k)+a(n−k)(2(n−k)+1)+(−1)n−r+1∑k=0r−1(r−1k)(b−a)k−n(c−b)n−k2c(n−k)+b(n−k)(2(n−k)+1)] \begin{align} E(X_{(r)}) &= r {n \choose r} \bigg[ \ \sum_{k=0}^{n-r} {n-r \choose k} (b-a)^{k-n} (c-a)^{n-k} (-1)^{n-r-k} \frac{2c(n-k)+a}{(n-k)(2(n-k) + 1)} \\ &+ (-1)^{n-r+1} \sum_{k=0}^{r-1} {r-1 \choose k} (b-a)^{k-n} (c-b)^{n-k} \frac{2c(n-k)+b}{(n-k)(2(n-k)+1)} \ \bigg] \end{align}

Expected Value of rthr^{th} order statistic squared

Continuing from the above derivation:

E(X(r)2)=γ0γ1n∑k=0n−r(n−rk)γ1k(−1)n−r−k∫acx2(x−a)2n−2k−1dx+γ0γ2n(−1)(n−r)∑k=0r−1(r−1k)γ2k∫cbx2(x−b)2n−2k−1dx \begin{align} E(X_{(r)}^2) &= \frac{\gamma_0}{\gamma_1^n} \sum_{k=0}^{n-r} {n-r \choose k} \gamma_1^k (-1)^{n-r-k}\int_a^c x^2(x-a)^{2n-2k-1}dx \\ &+ \frac{\gamma_0}{\gamma_2^n} (-1)^{(n-r)} \sum_{k=0}^{r-1} {r-1 \choose k} \gamma_2^k \int_c^b x^2(x-b)^{2n-2k-1}dx \end{align}

E(X(r)2)=γ0∑k=0n−r(n−rk)γ1k−n(−1)n−r−k(c−a)2n−2k2n−2k[c2−2c(c−a)2n−2k+1+2(c−a)2(2n−2k+1)(2n−2k+2)]+γ0(−1)(n−r)∑k=0r−1(r−1k)γ2k−n(c−b)2n−2k2n−2k[−c2+2c(c−b)2n−2k+1−2(c−b)2(2n−2k+1)(2n−2k+2)] \begin{align} E(X_{(r)}^2) &= \gamma_0 \sum_{k=0}^{n-r} {n-r \choose k} \gamma_1^{k-n} (-1)^{n-r-k} \frac{(c-a)^{2n-2k}}{2n-2k}\left[c^2 - \frac{2c(c-a)}{2n-2k+1} + \frac{2(c-a)^2}{(2n-2k+1)(2n-2k+2)}\right] \\ &+ \gamma_0 (-1)^{(n-r)} \sum_{k=0}^{r-1} {r-1 \choose k} \gamma_2^{k-n} \frac{(c-b)^{2n-2k}}{2n-2k}\left[-c^2 + \frac{2c(c-b)}{2n-2k+1}-\frac{2(c-b)^2}{(2n-2k+1)(2n-2k+2)}\right] \end{align}

E(X(r)2)=r(nr)∑k=0n−r(n−rk)(b−a)k−n(c−a)n−k(−1)n−r−k1n−k[c2−2c(c−a)2n−2k+1+2(c−a)2(2n−2k+1)(2n−2k+2)]+r(nr)(−1)(n−r)∑k=0r−1(r−1k)(b−a)k−n(c−b)n−k1n−k[−c2+2c(c−b)2n−2k+1−2(c−b)2(2n−2k+1)(2n−2k+2)] \begin{align} E(X_{(r)}^2) &= r {n \choose r} \sum_{k=0}^{n-r} {n-r \choose k} (b-a)^{k-n} (c-a)^{n-k} (-1)^{n-r-k} \frac{1}{n-k}\left[c^2 - \frac{2c(c-a)}{2n-2k+1} + \frac{2(c-a)^2}{(2n-2k+1)(2n-2k+2)}\right] \\ &+ r {n \choose r} (-1)^{(n-r)} \sum_{k=0}^{r-1} {r-1 \choose k} (b-a)^{k-n} (c-b)^{n-k} \frac{1}{n-k}\left[-c^2 + \frac{2c(c-b)}{2n-2k+1}-\frac{2(c-b)^2}{(2n-2k+1)(2n-2k+2)}\right] \end{align}

Variance of the rthr^{th} order statistic

V(X(r))=E(X(r)2)−[E(X(r))]2V\left(X_{(r)}\right) = E(X_{(r)}^2) - \left[E(X_{(r)})\right]^2

Numerical Stability of Variance and Expected value of rthr^{th} order statistic

Although the above derivation gives an exact solution to the variance and expected value of the rthr^{th} order statistic of the triangle distribution, the alternative sign inside the binomial sum and the large orders of magnitude over which those coefficients span lead to cancellation errors in the results that are not easy to solve. Exact solutions can be obtained to arbitrary precision through the use a package like Rmpfr. The triangle package defaults to the use of numerical integration for these results.

Logarithmic Triangle distribution

Define:

al=log⁡ϕ(a),bl=log⁡ϕ(b),cl=log⁡ϕ(c),h=2bl−al,ϕ=log basea_l=\log_{\phi}(a),\ \ b_l=\log_{\phi}(b),\ \ c_l=\log_{\phi}(c),\ \ h=\frac{2}{b_l-a_l}, \ \ \phi = \mbox{log base}

f(z)={hcl−al(z−al)if al≤z≤clhcl−bl(z−bl)if cl<z≤bl0otherwise(5)f(z) = \left\{ \begin{array}{ll} \frac{h}{c_l - a_l}(z - a_l) & \mbox{if } a_l \leq z \leq c_l \\ \frac{h}{c_l - b_l}(z - b_l) & \mbox{if } c_l < z \leq b_l \\ 0 & \mbox{otherwise} \end{array} \right.\ \ \ \ (5)

However,

E(ϕz)≠ϕE(z)(6)E({\phi}^z) \neq {\phi}^{E(z)}\ \ \ \ (6)

Therefore, transforming…

Y=ϕZY={\phi}^Z

Z=log⁡ϕ(Y)Z=\log_{\phi}(Y)

w(y)=log⁡ϕ(y)w(y)=\log_{\phi}(y)

w′(y)=dzdy=1ylog⁡(ϕ)w'(y)=\frac{dz}{dy} = \frac{1}{y\log({\phi})}

g(y)=f(w(y))w′(y)g(y)=f(w(y))w'(y)

g(y)={2(cl−al)(bl−al)log⁡(ϕ)logϕ(y)−alyif 0<a≤y≤c2(cl−bl)(bl−al)log⁡(ϕ)logϕ(y)−blyif c<y≤b0otherwise(7)g(y) = \left\{ \begin{array}{ll} \frac{2}{(c_l-a_l)(b_l-a_l)\log({\phi})}\frac{log_{\phi}(y) - a_l}{y} & \mbox{if } 0 < a \leq y \leq c \\ \frac{2}{(c_l-b_l)(b_l-a_l)\log({\phi})}\frac{log_{\phi}(y) - b_l}{y} & \mbox{if } c < y \leq b \\ 0 & \mbox{otherwise} \end{array} \right.\ \ \ \ (7)

Define:

β1=2(cl−al)(bl−al)\beta_1=\frac{2}{(c_l-a_l)(b_l-a_l)}

β2=2(cl−bl)(bl−al)\beta_2=\frac{2}{(c_l-b_l)(b_l-a_l)}

Finding the CDF,

G(y)=∫−∞yg(y)dyG(y) = \int_{-\infty}^y g(y)dy

fora≤y≤c,G(y)=β1log⁡(ϕ)∫aylog⁡(y)ylog⁡(ϕ)−alydy=β1[log⁡ϕ2(y)2−allog⁡ϕ(y)−al22+al2] \begin{align} \mbox{for}\ a \leq y \leq c,\ \ G(y) &= \frac{\beta_1}{\log({\phi})} \int_a^y \frac{\log(y)}{y\log({\phi})}-\frac{a_l}{y}dy \\ &=\beta_1 \bigg[\frac{\log_{\phi}^2(y)}{2} - a_l \log_{\phi}(y) - \frac{a_l^2}{2} + a_l^2\bigg] \end{align}

forc<y≤b,G(y)=G(c)+β2log⁡(ϕ)∫cylog⁡(y)ylog⁡(ϕ)−blydy=G(c)+β2[log⁡ϕ2(y)2−bllog⁡ϕ(y)−cl22+blcl] \begin{align} \mbox{for}\ c < y \leq b,\ \ G(y) &= G(c) + \frac{\beta_2}{\log({\phi})} \int_c^y \frac{\log(y)}{y\log({\phi})} - \frac{b_l}{y}dy \\ &=G(c) + \beta_2 \bigg[\frac{\log_{\phi}^2(y)}{2} - b_l \log_{\phi}(y) - \frac{c_l^2}{2} + b_l c_l\bigg] \end{align}

Checking that the CDF is 1 at b,

G(b)=cl2−2alcl+al2(cl−al)(bl−al)+−bl2−cl2+2blcl(cl−bl)(bl−al)=cl−albl−al+−(cl−bl)bl−al=1 \begin{align} G(b) &= \frac{c_l^2 - 2a_l c_l + a_l^2}{(c_l-a_l)(b_l-a_l)} + \frac{-b_l^2-c_l^2+2b_lc_l}{(c_l-b_l)(b_l-a_l)} \\ &= \frac{c_l-a_l}{b_l-a_l} + \frac{-(c_l-b_l)}{b_l-a_l} = 1 \end{align}

Now calculating E(y)E(y),

E(y)=∫yg(y)dy=β1log⁡(ϕ)∫ac[log⁡(y)log⁡(ϕ)−al]dy+β2log⁡(ϕ)∫cb[log⁡(y)log⁡(ϕ)−bl]dy=cβ1log⁡2(ϕ)[log⁡(c)−1−log⁡(a)+ac]+cβ2log⁡2(ϕ)[−bc−log⁡(c)+1+log⁡(b)] \begin{align} E(y) &= \int y\ g(y)\ dy \\ &=\frac{\beta_1}{\log({\phi})} \int_a^c \bigg[\frac{\log(y)}{\log({\phi})} - a_l\bigg]dy + \frac{\beta_2}{\log({\phi})} \int_c^b \bigg[\frac{\log(y)}{\log({\phi})} - b_l\bigg]dy \\ &=\frac{c\beta_1}{\log^2({\phi})} \bigg[\log(c) - 1 - \log(a) + \frac{a}{c} \bigg] + \frac{c\beta_2}{\log^2({\phi})} \bigg[\frac{-b}{c} - \log(c) + 1 + \log(b) \bigg] \end{align}
